chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Chester Chapp (Trader Horn) plans his own jazz funeral
summary: A rattan shop owner and music lover who ordered a band for his funeral and a party at a Greek restaurant.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Now, talking about strange things that happen to people. I don't know whether you remember this fellow, he had a basket shop up on North State Street.
Weave, right, right, right, and all kinds of things. We called him Trader Horn. He got that name from the old movie, years and years ago, Trader Horn. Anyway,

we were friends. He loved music. He didn't play anything, but if he wanted to hear something, he would go from here to Milwaukee or whatever, to hear what he wanted. He loved Roy and he loved the guys from that era. So he used to come to the Club Delisa. Unfortunately, he caught cancer and he was going to die. They told him he was terminal.

So he called me up one day, and he says, I want you to arrange my funeral for me. Says, I want you to get me -- how many pieces do I need? Just like he was hiring -- this was the most morbid thing, but, I mean, it stayed with me. So, anyway, it ended up that his -- somebody who was going to pay the bill, they contacted Bill Rinehart, but they still got me. I worked it for him. We played at his funeral, we played him into the --

Yeah, out of the funeral parlor into the -- what's the name, into the hearse. And after that, then he told us, he says, now, I want all of you to go over to the Greek restaurant over there, and just eat, drink and have a ball on me. And he said, -- but the way he originally wanted it, he wanted us to march from the funeral parlor to in front of his place over on State Street, there, and then with the band and just be playing in the street. He says, because I want them to know old Chester went out swinging.

Yeah. Chester Chapp was his name. Yeah. But what I'm saying is, you were talking about community and things and different things like that. With a musician, he's more or less -- I don't know them all, but I know in my position you become like a doctor or consultant or -- the whole bit.
